body_markdown:
In keeping with Spotify’s commitment to the mental health and well-being of music professionals, today we’re proud to announce our contribution to the


[Backline Treatment Grant](https://backline.care/dividedsky/) —


a


new program designed to remove the financial barrier to residential addiction recovery.


Created by


[Backline](https://backline.care/) , a mental health and wellness nonprofit for people in the music industry, and Divided Sky Foundation, a nonprofit residential recovery program founded by


[Phish](https://open.spotify.com/artist/5wbIWUzTPuTxTyG6ouQKqz) guitarist


**Trey Anastasio** , the grant is made possible through donations from


[Harper House Music Foundation](https://harperhousemusicfoundation.org/) and Spotify.


“Financial circumstances should never stand between someone and the chance to build a joyful life in recovery,” said


**Seth Dolinsky** , Executive Director of Divided Sky Foundation. “Thanks to Backline, Harper House Music Foundation, and Spotify, this grant gives music industry professionals and their families access to Divided Sky’s unique approach to recovery without the burden of program costs.”


The Backline Treatment Grant offers two programs, both hosted at


[Divided Sky’s residential retreat](https://dividedsky.org/) in Ludlow, Vermont, and takes an approach grounded in community, mindfulness, and the healing power of music.


The


**Recovery Recharge Program** is funded by Spotify and is our first expansion into substance use and recovery support. Music professionals who are at least one year into recovery can join the seven-day program, where they’ll have space to reconnect with their community, strengthen the recovery tools they’ve built, and return to their lives with renewed focus.


“Recovery Recharge is an incredible program that gives people the opportunity to really examine what a healthy, carefree, joyous sober life can look like,” said Trey. “I’m so grateful that Spotify and Backline are supporting Divided Sky and helping more musicians and the people around them not only maintain their sobriety, but experience the joy that comes with it.”


Meanwhile, the


**Residential Recovery Program** , funded by Harper House Music Foundation, is a 30-day program that gives people at the beginning of their recovery journey a chance to build a healthy foundation through the 12 Steps, emotional sobriety, mindfulness, and community.


## **Additional support for the music community**


Alongside the grant, Spotify, Backline, and Divided Sky are releasing a


[free sobriety guide](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RTzN2dX2ENlNfR_Wfhbi3P4AVWG-dbtF?usp=sharing) created specifically for music industry professionals.


We’re also funding a virtual educational session for live entertainment industry workers on December 17, hosted by the National Independent Venue Foundation (NIVF) and featuring experts from our partners at Backline and Divided Sky. Registration for the virtual session can be found


[here](https://www.nivf.org/event-registration-sobriety-in-live-entertainment) .


## **Supporting music professionals year-round** **** ****


This work builds on our ongoing support for the mental health and well-being of music industry professionals. Earlier this year, alongside Backline, we launched


[B-LINE](https://newsroom.spotify.com/2026-01-27/b-line-mental-health-hotline/) , a 24/7 mental health and crisis hotline. We’ve also worked with Backline to bring mental health and wellness resources to events like the


[Created by Women](https://newsroom.spotify.com/2026-09-24/created-by-women-summit/) and


[Fresh Finds Forward](https://newsroom.spotify.com/2026-11-02/fresh-finds-summit-los-angeles/) summits.


And last year, we expanded our


[Heart & Soul](https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-06-12/spotifys-heart-soul-initiative-brings-mental-health-support-to-artists-and-creators-worldwide/) initiative to artists, songwriters, and people within the music industry globally. Launched in 2018 for Spotify employees, the program now gives creators around the world access to mental health resources that help them thrive.


Together, these programs reflect our commitment to helping music industry professionals find the support they need, when they need it.


*Learn more about the Backline Treatment Grant*[here](https://backline.care/dividedsky/) *.*
